done_when: The commit hook refuses only when git commit itself is given -n or --no-verify, never for an -n that belongs to another command on the same line

findings.body: Raise: Security. The heredoc search treats `<<EOF` inside a quoted argument as a real heredoc opener. For the valid shell input `echo '<<EOF'` followed on the next line by `git commit -n`, it discards the commit line before the guard inspects it. The hook therefore permits a commit that skips Git hooks.
findings.title: Literal heredoc marker can hide a prohibited commit

findings.body: Raise: Not done. Lines 193–194 restore every heredoc body whenever the retained text contains `bash`, even if that word is only in the commit message. A valid `git commit -F - <<'EOF'` message that says `Fix bash hook handling` and later mentions `git commit -n` is refused, although the invoked commit has no prohibited option. The allowed heredoc tests do not contain a shell name in their messages.

findings.body: Raise: Test. The changed test calls `forge hook deny` directly in the manually initialized `repo` fixture. It does not exercise the corrected decision through a newly initialized client or a client adopted on an earlier release and then upgraded. The existing upgrade test checks that host configuration contains `forge hook deny`, but does not check this flag behavior. The repository's review rule requires tests covering both client lifecycles.
findings.title: Not done: init and earlier-adoption upgrade tests for the corrected hook

why: The commit hook treats pytest -n 2 on the same command line as git commit as skipping the hooks and refuses the commit
